chapter_title: Chương 296: 0298【Hàn Quốc bắt đầu bôi nhọ Game Science】

segments.title: Chương 296: 0298【Hàn Quốc bắt đầu bôi nhọ Game Science】
segments.content:
The employees of ByteDance returned after the New Year to find an accounting team permanently stationed in the office, and everyone began guessing when the company could successfully go public.

Just three days after the Lantern Festival, the initial due diligence and planning report was placed before Chen Guiliang. The company's financial compliance had to be rectified based on this document.

There were few major problems, but quite a few minor loopholes.

For the next period, the accounting team would come three or four days a week, gradually correcting one problem after another.

Zhihu had already set up its website but hadn't started promoting it yet.

The product manager in charge of Zhihu was named Lu Jie, a graduate of Renmin University who had joined ByteDance after its Series A financing. He started by organizing small activities on Xiaonei Wang, then later moved to Hainei Wang to do event planning.

"Boss, this is the positioning and development strategy for Zhihu that we've discussed."

Lu Jie handed over the proposal and briefly explained its contents, "Since we need to differentiate ourselves from Xiaonei Wang groups, Baidu Tieba, Baidu Q&A, and Tianya Laiba, we might as well make the distinction more radical."

Chen Guiliang asked while reading the proposal, "What's your plan?"

Lu Jie said, "In its early operational phase, Zhihu will be registration-by-invitation-code-only. Company executives and project team members will distribute invitation codes through their real-life social networks. The invitees must either be graduates of prestigious universities or authorities in their professional fields."

Chen Guiliang smiled as he listened.

Lu Jie continued, "We shouldn't expand too quickly at the start. If an invitee registers on Zhihu, they will automatically be issued one invitation code per week, so they can invite their friends. At the same time, we'll issue them additional codes based on the acceptance rate and number of their answers."

"In addition, we will randomly select five people from Hainei Wang and Xiaonei Wang each week to receive invitation codes. They'll need to fill out an application form first to be eligible for the draw."

"Guests without an account can also visit Zhihu. But guests cannot register or post, they can only browse silently."

"We also have to prevent registered users from spamming. After multiple warnings are ignored, their posting privileges will be suspended for a period of time."

"We need to build Zhihu into a high-end knowledge community, making Zhihu's invitation codes highly sought after and difficult to obtain. We want countless people to wish they could join but be unable to, forced to browse the Q&A content as guests every day."

"This way, we will be completely different from other knowledge communities. It will make Zhihu unique among similar websites and greatly enhance user stickiness. Once our reputation is established, we can gradually increase the issuance of invitation codes until we choose the right moment to open up registration."

Chen Guiliang stared at Lu Jie for a few moments, really wanting to ask: Are you a reincarnator too?

In truth, this wasn't Lu Jie's idea alone, but the result of discussions with his entire team.

Similar websites and communities already existed, and since Zhihu was created relatively late, it had to compete through differentiation. If they were going to differentiate, they might as well take it to the extreme.

Chen Guiliang became the first registered user and casually posted a ridiculous question: "The feasibility and mechanical analysis of tiling the Great Wall."

Immediately after, he called the 72-year-old Professor Huang.

Professor Huang had been elected an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences four years ago and was currently a doctoral supervisor at Peking University. When Qian Xuesen returned to China and began teaching, Professor Huang was one of those first 15 students.

After some coaxing from Chen Guiliang, Professor Huang actually agreed to register, thinking it would be a nice way to change gears in his spare time.

Not only was he an expert in high-tech fields, but he also genuinely had some research knowledge in architecture. Seeing Chen Guiliang's question about tiling the Great Wall, Professor Huang analyzed it from the perspectives of project scale and cost, technical difficulty, cultural relic preservation, environmental impact, maintenance costs, and various mechanical angles.

The final conclusion: zero feasibility.

Professor Huang grew happier and happier as he wrote at home that night, because this sort of thing didn't tax his brain, yet it was still a serious discussion of a problem. He wrote over three thousand words in one go, even including many calculation processes...

The next day, Professor Huang even told his doctoral students about it.

In between their research projects, the doctoral students went to Zhihu as guests to check it out. They burst out laughing when they saw Professor Huang's answer.

Meanwhile, more than 30 questions had already appeared on Zhihu, and over half of them had been answered.

All of them were highly professional and in-depth answers!

The respondents were all well-known figures from various industries!

There weren't just questions on science and engineering, but also many real-world questions from the humanities. For example, how to become a host at CCTV, and what basic skills are required for a CCTV host, which Chen Guiliang managed to get Xiao Cui to answer after pulling some strings.

The doctoral students felt like they had discovered a treasure trove of a website and started asking how they could register, only to be told they needed an invitation code.

There were only two ways to get an invitation code.

First, by filling out an application form through a Xiaonei Wang or Hainei Wang account, with five people being selected each week to receive codes. (Although it was said to be a random draw, priority was actually given to those with higher education and deeper qualifications.)

Second, by getting an invitation code from a friend.

The doctoral students hurried to Professor Huang, only to have him say that he only got one invitation code per week. His number of answers and acceptance rate would be calculated monthly, and then additional codes would be issued according to the standard.

The doctoral students were speechless. Was it this hard just to register for an account on a website?

Professor Huang, however, found it quite interesting. He directly used the invitation code as a reward, giving priority to the doctoral student in his research group who performed the best.

Within certain small circles, Zhihu's reputation spread rapidly.

In contrast to Zhihu's slow development, Tianya Laiba was expanding at a furious pace.

It was a pure imitation of Baidu Tieba, using keywords from Google searches to form one related community after another.

However, the hidden dangers were immense.

The co-president system at Google China had finally produced a result in its power struggle.

Kai-Fu Lee had forced the other president to resign voluntarily at the end of last year.

Then, Google China went back on its word and began to vie for control of Tianya Laiba—why should I honor a promise made by my competitor? He's already resigned, so if you have a problem, go find him.

Tianya could only grit its teeth and accept it.

Because Google was still a shareholder in Tianya, having invested before their collaboration began, and it also provided technical support to Tianya.

One week after school started, ByteDance and Game Science launched their first-ever campus recruitment plan.

For now, it was only open to major universities in Beijing, and ByteDance was only hiring 20 people, while Game Science was hiring only 15.

Spring and fall recruitment seasons had been around since about the year 2000.

Chen Guiliang's two companies didn't even hold recruitment seminars on campus; they simply created a special Beijing campus recruitment section on Xiaonei Wang.

You had to be a Xiaonei Wang user first before you could submit your resume to Chen Guiliang's companies!

"Damn, I finally passed CET-4!"

Chen Guiliang received his score for the College English Test Band 4 he took at the end of last year.

The passing score was 425, and Chen Guiliang scored 503.

Well above the passing line.

In fact, even if he hadn't crammed, he likely would have passed by guessing.

Our CEO Chen might be weak in spoken English and listening, but as a rural "exam whiz," his test-taking skills were still outstanding.

"CEO Chen, let's have dinner this weekend to celebrate our housewarming," Ao Yanchen said, coming into his office just after work started in the morning.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Just you?"

Ao Yanchen said, "A few of us executives from ByteDance and Game Science bought houses together last year. After they were decorated and aired out for a few months, we moved in after coming back for the Spring Festival this year."

Chen Guiliang said, "Alright, give me a call then."

Just as Ao Yanchen left, Huang Xinyuan, who was in charge of the SP business, came in.

Huang Xinyuan said, "The operators are making big moves again. After a series of measures like the secondary confirmation, they're now tightening billing channels and adjusting settlement rules..."

"They're also implementing a credit score management system, deducting credit points from companies with too many complaints. Once a score is too low, their services will be suspended directly, and any unsettled payments will be frozen. In the most severe cases, their SP business license will be revoked entirely."

"SP service codes are being unified across the four networks, with companies like China Mobile and China Unicom implementing standardized supervision..."

"The Ministry of Information Industry has also joined forces with the operators to launch a cleanup campaign. I heard the fines can be as high as several million yuan..."

This combination of blows was enough to knock many SP service providers senseless.

The industry leader in color ringtones, TOM Online, was hit so hard by the crackdown that it delisted from NASDAQ and Hong Kong. Others like Hurray! and Linktone were either forced to transform or undergo asset restructuring.

These SP service providers had all been extremely profitable enterprises before, engaging in all sorts of deceptive consumption and illicit operations.

The state's crackdown on the wireless value-added services sector was tantamount to wringing their necks.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Will the state take action this time against the SP service providers that infringe on color ringtone copyrights?"
